## Data Cleaning

Rows with empty cells were removed. Strings were converted into numbers. Release decade column was added.

```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
data <- read.csv("Most Streamed Spotify Songs 2024.csv")

# Remove rows with empty cells
data[data == ""] <- NA
clean_data <- data %>% drop_na(Track, Album.Name, Artist, Release.Date, ISRC, 
                               Spotify.Streams, Spotify.Playlist.Count,
                               Spotify.Popularity, YouTube.Views, YouTube.Likes,
                               TikTok.Posts,TikTok.Likes, 
                               TikTok.Views, YouTube.Playlist.Reach,
                               Explicit.Track)

# Convert strings into numbers
cols <- c("Spotify.Streams", "Spotify.Playlist.Count", "Spotify.Playlist.Reach",
          "YouTube.Views", "YouTube.Likes", "TikTok.Posts",
          "TikTok.Likes", "TikTok.Views")

clean_data[cols] <- lapply(clean_data[cols], function(x) {
  x <- gsub(",", "", x)
  as.numeric(x)
})

# Add release decade column 
clean_data$Release.Date <- as.Date(clean_data$Release.Date, format = "%m/%d/%Y")
clean_data$Release.Year <- as.numeric(format(clean_data$Release.Date, "%Y"))
clean_data$Release.Decade <- cut(
  clean_data$Release.Year,
  breaks = c(1900, 2009, 2019, 2029),
  labels = c("Pre-2010s", "2010s", "2020s")
)
```
